newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lockheed in Australian radar project.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lockheed in Australian radar project.

text.p: Australian telecommunications group Telstra Corp said on Monday that Lockheed Martin Corp and the unlisted Transfield Defence Systems will manage Telstra's Jindalee radar defence project through to completion.

Telstra said the two companies had formed a joint venture firm to manage the Jindalee Operational Radar Network (JORN) and will acquire a Telstra unit called Telstar which is a key contractor to the project.
Lockheed currently owns 40 percent of Telstar and will have a 50 percent stake in the joint venture. Terms were not disclosed, with the agreement set to take effect in early 1997.

"The JORN project is considered one of Australia's largest defence contracts and, on completion, will give Australia a new level of defence security," Telstra said. "JORN is an operational wide area surveillance system of skywave over the horizon radars. Initially it will comprise two radars at Longreach in Queensland and Laverton in Western Australia."

The Australian government said earlier this year it was concerned about delays to the A$1.1 billion project after being told by Telstra that it faced a three year delay in starting the the project, now due for about the year 2000.
